definition: A trade that relies on a trader's physical ability to store natural gas over short periods, buying when demand and price are low and reselling when demand and price are high.
core_idea: Because gas demand fluctuates significantly even within a week, a trader with storage access can buy inexpensive gas during low-demand periods and resell it during high-demand periods.
key_points: Pipelines operate continuously, but gas demand varies considerably over short periods such as a week.
Example: Monday mornings see high demand from industrial restarts and reheating offices after the weekend; late Saturday night sees low demand (no industrial demand, less home heating).
Executing this strategy requires the physical ability to store natural gas.
relationships: A type of spread-like trade distinct from spread trades proper
Distinct from swing swaps/options, which are financial derivatives sharing a similar name
trading_implications: Only accessible to traders/entities with physical storage access.
caveats: "Swing trade" (physical storage arbitrage) should not be confused with "swing swap"/"swing option" (financial derivatives with daily delivery flexibility).
